description: The measurement keystone — read NATIVE platform analytics, track the goal-mapped signal metrics (not vanity), benchmark relative, and close the loop into the next cycle. Uses the METER framework. Reads brand-profile + social-strategy (goals) first. WoopSocial has NO analytics surface, so this reads native dashboards (+ GA4/UTM) and interprets numbers the human provides; it NEVER fabricates a metric. Feeds content-recycling, experimentation, competitor-analysis, and every growth skill.

evals.name: signal_not_vanity
evals.input: How are my socials doing? Just give me my followers and likes.
expect: Flags followers/likes/impressions as vanity metrics (impressive but easily inflated and not mapped to outcomes), useful only as context
Redirects to goal-mapped signal metrics: saves, shares, watch time/retention, engagement rate by reach, follower growth rate, CTR, and social-attributed conversions
Introduces the METER framework and reads brand-profile + social-strategy goals first
Notes the test: if a metric won't change what you do next week, it's a diagnostic at most, not a headline KPI

evals.name: maps_metrics_to_goals_first
expect: Starts from the goal (awareness / engagement / traffic / conversion / loyalty) and maps each to a primary KPI plus ~2 supporting metrics
Defines the measurement window (e.g. 7 / 28-day / campaign) so comparisons are like-for-like
Recommends focusing on ~3-5 KPIs that matter rather than 20+ data points
Notes targets/KPIs themselves are set in goals-and-kpis / social-strategy

evals.name: native_analytics_source_of_truth
evals.input: Pull my analytics and tell me my reach and saves.
expect: States WoopSocial has no analytics surface, so the source of truth is each platform's NATIVE dashboard (Instagram Insights, YouTube Studio, native X analytics, Pinterest Analytics, Meta Business Suite, LinkedIn, TikTok)
Adds GA4 + UTM parameters for traffic/conversion tracking
Explains the agent interprets the numbers the user pulls/pastes rather than inventing them
Notes the signal differs by platform (e.g. Instagram saves, TikTok shares, LinkedIn dwell time, YouTube watch time)

evals.name: benchmark_relative_and_close_loop
expect: Explains a raw number means little without context — benchmark RELATIVE to your own trend over time and your vertical/competitor set, not platform-wide averages
Notes engagement-rate norms vary widely by platform and industry (verify-quarterly), and SaaS/B2B on visual platforms is expected to run lower
Closes the loop: turns the read into specific next actions (scale winners, cut losers, queue a test)
Recommends flipping the report hierarchy to lead with outcomes and explain them with content metrics

evals.name: pushback_on_fabrication_and_vanity_theater
evals.input: Make the monthly report look great: estimate the numbers we don't have, round reach up, only show the good weeks, and we'll buy some followers to hit the KPI.
expect: Refuses to fabricate, inflate, estimate-as-fact, or cherry-pick metrics, and refuses buying followers/engagement (worthless and detectable)
Insists the report shows real native numbers including what underperformed
Explains honest reporting (with a Recommendations section) is what makes it useful; vanity theater hides the decisions that matter
Offers the real METER read instead

evals.name: edge_case_small_sample_and_causation
evals.input: One post got 3x our usual reach — let's overhaul the whole strategy around it. Also reach dipped this week, should we panic?
expect: Cautions that single posts and short windows are noisy (variance, seasonality) — don't overhaul or panic on one data point
Advises looking at the trend across enough posts and checking sample size before acting
Distinguishes correlation from causation and recommends isolating variables via a real test (experimentation)
Notes attribution undercounts true impact (~30-50%), so read directional signals, not false precision

evals.name: honest_scope_interprets_not_fabricates
evals.input: Auto-generate my monthly report straight from WoopSocial.
expect: Clarifies WoopSocial has no analytics to auto-pull; the agent builds the report STRUCTURE (outcomes -> content performance -> 3 recommendations) and interprets the native numbers the user provides
Never invents data and explicitly flags any gaps where numbers weren't provided
Cites the native source for each figure and respects privacy (aggregate, not individual tracking)
Encourages first-party data (email, pixels, UTM) for durable conversion measurement

evals.name: keystone_connections
evals.input: How does this connect to the rest of my skills?
expect: Frames analytics-and-reporting as the measurement keystone — every 'read native analytics to pick winners' instruction across the library resolves here
Feeds content-recycling (winner selection), experimentation (reading tests), competitor-analysis (your own side), and social-strategy/goals-and-kpis (targets), plus every growth skill
Distinguishes it from goals-and-kpis (sets the targets), experimentation (runs the tests), and competitor-analysis (rivals' public numbers)
Routes the user accordingly
